entries.description: use Suffix/Prefix/Middle pattern for infill (instead of Prefix/Suffix/Middle) as some models prefer this. (default: disabled)
entries.notes: Accepted on both server binaries through the shared `mlxcel::cli::infill_args::InfillArgs` group and honored by POST /infill: the flag moves the suffix block ahead of the prefix block while the middle marker stays last, which is upstream's swap exactly. b10621 declares it value-less with no environment binding, so this definition has none either. `infill_route_tests.rs::spm_infill_changes_the_prompt_the_server_actually_sends` asserts the flag reaches the served prompt rather than only the config.

The former mlxcel-native rich health payload moved to GET /slots and GET /metrics.

Renders a chat-completions body through the loaded chat template and answers {"prompt": "..."} without generating. The render is the same `prepare_chat_request_with_cache` call /v1/chat/completions makes, so messages, tools, reasoning options and chat_template_kwargs are honored and what comes back is the prompt that request would have been served with. The MAX_TOOLS guard runs first, as it does on the generating routes, so an oversized tool array cannot reach Jinja2 through a route that does not generate.

Answers {"input_tokens": N} for a chat-completions body. The count runs the same render and the same encode the generation path runs (encode(prompt, add_special=true)), so it is the number of tokens that request would really have been prefilled with rather than an estimate that can drift from it.

Route separation done: /completion and /completions both reach the native handler and answer the b10621 native object (index, content, tokens, id_slot, stop, model, tokens_predicted, tokens_evaluated, generation_settings, prompt, has_new_line, truncated, stop_type, stopping_word, tokens_cached, timings with cache_n), and the streaming form ends with that same object rather than a [DONE] sentinel. The key set and order were taken from a capture of the pinned binary. #1466 closed the stop-sequence half; #1441 added `response_fields`, `stream_options`, the whole `n_predict` value domain and the real prefill figures on every streaming frame; #1525 settled `tokens_cached` (the slot occupancy `tokens_evaluated + tokens_predicted - 1`) and `verbose` (accepted and inert, because upstream emits `__verbose` only from its OAI-compat builders). #1477 closed the request-field remainder: `return_tokens`, `return_progress`, `n_indent` and `t_max_predict_ms` are honored against upstream's measured rules, and `generation_settings` grew from 39 to 47 of upstream's 49 `task_params` keys. The streaming frames also match upstream's per-token cadence now: one frame per decoded token, carrying that token's id in `tokens` unconditionally and the slot's generated-token count in `tokens_predicted`, with the -1 `id_slot` sentinel upstream stamps on every partial frame and the real slot id on the final one only. `n_cmpl` above 1 stays refused (`field:n_cmpl`), which is byte-equivalent to upstream's own refusal at one slot. What remains is the two permanent differences in divergence, each with a rationale and a pinning test.
divergence: `generation_settings` reports 47 of b10621's 49 `task_params` keys: `backend_sampling` and `speculative.types` are omitted rather than invented, because mlxcel's sampler IS the backend graph with no CPU chain to switch to (`field:backend_sampling`) and mlxcel has no draft-model type to name. This is the omitted-rather-than-invented policy `GET /props` records (#1477).

When generation ends while the stop matcher is still holding a partial stop-string match, mlxcel emits the held text as a final content frame so the streamed concatenation equals the non-streaming `content`; b10621 drops it from the stream and keeps it in the body. Measured on the pinned binary with `stop: [" Paris.XYZ"]` and `n_predict: 2`: the streamed concatenation is empty while the non-streaming `content` is ` Paris.` (#1477).

rationale.reason: Both differences are the epic's own rules applied to this route. Reporting a `task_params` key mlxcel does not act on would tell a client a setting steers generation when it steers nothing, which is the silent-ignore misrepresentation epic #1431 exists to remove; the policy is self-correcting, and #1477 is the demonstration, moving eight keys (samplers, timings_per_token, logit_bias, lora, chat_format, generation_prompt, reasoning_format, reasoning_in_content) out of the omitted set as mlxcel gained an analogue for each. The held-tail flush is #1466's invariant that the concatenation of the streamed pieces equals the non-streaming text, which one funnel (`SequenceInfo::stream_decoded_text`) gives every serving path at once; upstream loses that text from its stream, and matching it would mean dropping output a client asked for.
rationale.revisit_if: mlxcel growing an analogue for `backend_sampling` or a draft-model type name for `speculative.types` moves that key into the reported set on its own, exactly as the eight keys #1477 added did. The held-tail flush would be revisited only if a b10621 client is found to depend on the stream ending short of the body, which would make losing the text the compatible behavior.

entries.notes: Special tokens are rendered rather than skipped, as upstream's `tokens_to_str` does, and an absent or empty `tokens` answers {"content": ""} rather than failing. Bytes that cannot form a character come back as U+FFFD, which is what upstream emits too because its JSON writer runs with the replacing error handler.

The native shape (a bare JSON array of {index, embedding} whose embedding is an array OF arrays) landed with #1441 and was verified against a capture of the pinned binary; #1452 closed the rest. The handler accepts upstream's legacy `content` spelling for the input and answers a body carrying neither key with upstream's own "input\" or \"content\" must be provided" sentence, reads the per-request `embd_normalize` over the whole b10621 domain, and the 501 body now opens with upstream's "This server does not support embeddings. Start it with `--embeddings`" because that flag really is accepted here.

Mounted and serving. The capability gate runs first and refuses a model whose vocabulary has no prefix, suffix and middle token with upstream's own wording, over the same spelling list llama-vocab.cpp scans; `input_prefix` and `input_suffix` are required, `input_extra` is validated as an array of {filename, text}, and the assembled prompt follows format_infill's ordering in both the default and --spm-infill forms. Two observable differences remain, recorded below; both are deliberate and permanent, which is what by_design records. The marker refusal is pinned by a_marker_in_the_prefix_is_refused_with_an_actionable_diagnostic and the untruncated FIM context by the_whole_fim_context_is_served_without_batch_truncation.
divergence: Text in input_prefix, input_suffix, input_extra[].text, input_extra[].filename or prompt that contains one of the model's own FIM marker spellings is refused with a diagnostic; b10621 tokenizes those fields with parse_special off and serves the marker as literal text. mlxcel's generation entry takes a prompt string that is re-tokenized with parsing on, so the marker would otherwise silently restructure the prompt.

The FIM context is not truncated to the prefill batch: b10621 keeps only the last 3*(n_batch/4) prefix tokens and the first (n_batch/4) - (2 + prompt) suffix tokens, while mlxcel serves the whole prefix and suffix, consistent with its policy of clamping an over-long request rather than dropping prompt text.

rationale.reason: mlxcel's generation entry takes a prompt string that is re-tokenized with special-token parsing on, so a string cannot express 'these characters are not that token'; refusing FIM-marker text beats letting a file the client did not write silently restructure the prompt. Serving the whole FIM context follows mlxcel's policy everywhere else of clamping an over-long request rather than dropping prompt text.
rationale.revisit_if: mlxcel's generation entry grows a parse_special-off prompt path (which would let marker text be served literally, as b10621 does), or the clamp-rather-than-drop policy for over-long requests is itself revisited.

entries.notes: All four aliases mounted (#1430); #1452 aligned the envelope. The Jina response now carries b10621's top-level "object": "list", and a request that spells its document list `texts` gets b10621's TEI shape instead: a bare array of {index, score} with `text` echoed under `return_text`. The Cohere `documents` / `return_documents` / `document` spelling mlxcel already served keeps working, and a body carrying both list spellings stays on the Jina envelope. The three shape errors use upstream's own wording. The route is served exactly when the operator asked for reranking; mlxcel spells that request as `--reranking`, `--pooling rank`, `--reranker-model <path>`, or a reranker checkpoint in -m, and the 501 body opens with upstream's "This server does not support reranking. Start it with `--reranking`".
The /reranking spelling of POST /rerank; all four paths reach one handler. See POST /rerank.

Answers {"input_tokens": N} for a Responses body. The body is flattened to the chat shape by the same translator /v1/responses uses, including previous_response_id and conversation rehydration, so the count covers the whole conversation the generation call would have prefilled rather than only the new turn.

All four b10621 switches are honored: `content` accepts the mixed shape (a string, or an array whose elements are strings or already-tokenized ids) and may be absent, in which case the answer is an empty token list rather than an error; `add_special` defaults to false; `parse_special` defaults to true and, when false, stops a special-token spelling written into the text from being recognized as that token; `with_pieces` switches the response to {id, piece} objects whose `piece` is a JSON string for valid UTF-8 and an array of byte values otherwise, so a token carrying part of a multi-byte character reassembles exactly.

entries.description: Number of completions to generate. If the input has multiple prompts, total outputs will be N prompts times n_cmpl
entries.notes: Declared and refused above 1 with a diagnostic naming the field. Upstream's schema limit is 1 <= value <= params_base.n_parallel and it REFUSES rather than clamps, so at one slot mlxcel's refusal is the same answer b10621 gives: the pinned binary with -np 1 answers `Field 'n_cmpl': Value must be between 1 <= value <= 1, but got 2`. With more slots upstream returns a JSON array of result objects each carrying its own index, and mlxcel serves one completion per request with no path that returns an array; shipping a partial array shape would be worse than the refusal (#1477).
divergence: above 1 the field is refused; b10621 with more than one slot returns a JSON array of result objects, which mlxcel has no path to produce

entries.description: Specify the minimum line indentation for the generated text in number of whitespace characters. Useful for code completion tasks
entries.notes:
Accepted and honored, as a per-request stop rule on the sequence (`GenerationBounds`). Upstream's rule (`server-context.cpp` `process_token`): once a newline has been generated and the cursor has advanced past it, the whitespace run at `last_nl_pos` is measured each step, and if the line has a character after that run and the run is shorter than `n_indent` the slot stops with STOP_TYPE_LIMIT and the text is erased from the first character after the run. mlxcel transcribes the walk including its one-line-per-token cursor advance, which is what makes the stopping token count agree rather than only the stopping text. Measured on the pinned binary with `seed: 7, temperature: 0` on `def f():
    x = 1
`: `n_indent: 0` runs the full 60 tokens, `n_indent: 4` stops at 24 with `stop_type: "limit"` and content ending `    print("done")
`, cut because the next line was empty. The value domain is upstream's hard limits 0..=2147483647, refused rather than clamped outside them.

entries.description: Set the maximum number of tokens to predict. When 0, no tokens will be generated but the prompt is evaluated into the cache
entries.notes: Accepted through the b10621 spelling and its `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` aliases, over upstream's whole value domain rather than serde's. The `n_predict: 0` prompt-only case is now verified rather than assumed: the pinned binary emits exactly ONE token for it (not zero, despite the schema description), evaluates the whole prompt and reports `stop_type: "limit"`, and mlxcel answers the same one token on the same prompt against a real checkpoint. `-1`, upstream's spelling of "as many as the context allows", is accepted and clamped to the effective context window instead of being refused with a 422 as it was before. A value outside `[-1, INT32_MAX]` is refused with upstream's own wording, `Field 'n_predict': Value must be between -1 <= value <= 2147483647, but got -2`. An in-domain value is still silently clamped to the effective per-slot context window, which is what upstream does too.

entries.description: A list of response fields to return. Missing fields are omitted without error. Fields with a slash are unnested (e.g. generation_settings/n_predict moves n_predict to the root)
entries.notes: Implemented against the pinned binary rather than against the schema's own description, which is wrong about what the binary does. Upstream walks each path through the finished response splitting on `/` and stores the value under the WHOLE path string, so `generation_settings/n_predict` comes back as a root key literally named "generation_settings/n_predict"; it does not move `n_predict` to the root the way the description claims. Captured and reproduced: a missing path is omitted without an error, a path that walks into a non-object is omitted, `[""]` selects nothing, a repeated path yields one key, a nested object can be selected whole, the result keeps the order the request listed, and an empty list or a value that is not an array of strings (`"content"`, `["content", 5]`, `null`) returns the whole object with a 200 rather than a type error. Applied to the non-streaming body and to the final streaming frame only, which is also where upstream applies it: the per-token frames are unprojected on both sides.

entries.description: Include prompt processing progress events in stream mode
entries.notes: Accepted and honored. Upstream's gate is `params.stream && params.return_progress`, so the field is inert on a non-streaming request: measured on the pinned binary, `{"return_progress": true}` without `stream` returns the same top-level key set as the request without it and no `prompt_progress`. On a streaming request upstream sends one empty-content frame when the slot starts processing and one per batch iteration after that, each carrying `prompt_progress: {total, cache, processed, time_ms}`; measured on a 4001-token prompt with the default batch, the processed values were 0, 2048, 4001 against total 4001, and on a repeat of the same prompt they were 4000, 4001 against `cache: 4000`, so `processed` counts cache-supplied tokens rather than starting at zero. mlxcel emits the same cadence: one observation when prefill starts (reporting what the prefix cache supplied) and one per evaluated prefill chunk, through the existing `GenerateEvent::Prefill` channel, which now carries `processed` and distinguishes a progress observation from the first-token snapshot. The opening frame is emitted on the padded batched cohort too, which is the dispatch two concurrent requests take by default.

entries.description: Return the raw generated token ids in the `tokens` field
entries.notes: Accepted and honored. The non-streaming `tokens` array carries the raw sampled ids when the field is set and is empty otherwise, which is upstream's own gate (`slot.generated_tokens` is only appended to under `return_tokens`, and `send_final_response` moves it into the result). Measured on the pinned binary: `The capital of France is` answered with 8 tokens returns `tokens: [12095, 13, 576, 6722, 315, 15344, 374, 21718]` against `tokens_predicted: 8`, and the same request without the field returns `[]`. The ids come from the scheduler (`SequenceInfo::generated_tokens`, carried out on `GenerationResult::generated_token_ids`) rather than from re-tokenizing the answer, because a string stop sequence excludes its matched text from `content` while its token still counts: with `stop: ["Paris"]` the binary answers `content: " "`, `tokens: [12095]`, `tokens_predicted: 1`. STREAMING frames carry a per-frame `tokens` array unconditionally, with and without the field, and the final streaming frame carries `tokens: []`; mlxcel matches, carrying the id on `TokenMeta` alongside each decoded piece. A backend that emits text spans with no 1:1 decoded token (the diffusion worker, the Florence-2 renderer) reports no ids, which is why `TokenMeta` is an option rather than a value.

entries.description: Allows receiving each predicted token in real-time instead of waiting for the completion to finish
Whether to include usage information in the stream
entries.notes: Declared and type-checked instead of being dropped as an unknown key. Measured on the pinned binary serving a real checkpoint: on the native `/completion` route the block is inert, because the native final frame already carries `tokens_predicted`, `tokens_evaluated` and the whole `timings` object whether or not it is sent, so a request with `{"include_usage": true}` and one without it answer byte-identical bodies. A non-object value (`"stream_options": "garbage"`) is tolerated and ignored on both sides. mlxcel's OpenAI routes honor the same block the way b10621's do, emitting the trailing usage chunk with empty `choices`; that half predates this epic.

The subfield of the block above, modeled by the nested `NativeStreamOptions` struct so its type is validated rather than the value being read past. A present non-boolean is refused with upstream's own wording, `Field 'include_usage': type must be boolean, but is string`, measured against the pinned binary; absent or `null` resolves to the upstream default of false. The value has no observable effect on `/completion` in either implementation.

entries.description: Set a time limit in milliseconds for the prediction phase. The timeout triggers if generation exceeds this time (measured since the first token) and a newline has been generated. Useful for FIM applications
entries.notes: Accepted and honored, as a per-request deadline on the sequence (`GenerationBounds`), distinct from the server-wide `--decode-timeout` watchdog, which is unchanged. Upstream's rule (`server-context.cpp` `process_token`): the deadline is armed and checked only on a piece whose EMITTED text contains a newline, and if the time since the first token has passed it the slot stops with STOP_TYPE_LIMIT. Measured on the pinned binary: `t_max_predict_ms: 50` on an `n_predict: 200` poem request stopped at 10 tokens with `stop_type: "limit"` and `predicted_ms: 52.488`, while the same request with `t_max_predict_ms: 0` ran the full 200. The value domain is upstream's hard limits -1..=9223372036854775807, with -1 and 0 both disabling it.

entries.description: Include prompt processing and text generation speed information in each response
entries.notes: Accepted and honored: a streaming frame carries the timing block when it is set and omits it otherwise. The per-frame block now reports the real prefill figures rather than zeros. A one-shot prefill snapshot (`GenerateEvent::Prefill`, emitted by the scheduler when the first token is stamped) reaches the streaming route before the first frame, so `cache_n`, `prompt_n`, `prompt_ms` and `tokens_evaluated` carry the same values on every frame that the final frame reports, which is what the pinned binary does. Two derivations inside the block were also corrected against the binary in the same change: `prompt_n` is `tokens_evaluated - cache_n` (a fully cached prefix reports `prompt_n: 1` against `tokens_evaluated: 8` with `cache_n: 7`), and the generation rates divide by `predicted_n - 1` because `predicted_ms` starts at the first token, so `predicted_n: 4` with `predicted_ms: 15.132` reports `predicted_per_token_ms: 5.044`.

entries.description: Include __verbose field in the response with additional debug information
entries.notes: Accepted and inert, which is exactly what b10621 does on this route. Upstream writes its __verbose debug block only from the OAI-compat response builders (server-task.cpp lines 404, 452, 521 and 1098, each inside a to_json_oaicompat* function); the native completion object IS to_json_non_oaicompat(), so the field changes nothing there. Measured against the pinned binary: the top-level key set of a request with verbose true is identical to the same request without it. Before #1477 mlxcel refused the field with a 400, which was the divergence.
